items.q: Mei is 4th in the line. Which sentence is true?
options: 3 children are in front of Mei.
4 children are in front of Mei.
5 children are in front of Mei.
items.answer: 3 children are in front of Mei.
steps: The places before 4th are 1st, 2nd and 3rd.
So 3 children are in front of Mei.
The line may be longer, so we cannot say how many are behind.

a: 4 children are in front of Mei.
slips.say: 4 is Mei's place. Count only the children in front of her.

items.q: There are 8 children in a line. Aisha is 3rd from the front. What place is Aisha from the back? Type just the number.
items.hint: Count from the back end: 1st, 2nd, and so on, up to Aisha.
steps: Aisha is 3rd from the front, so 2 children are in front of her.
The other 5 children are behind her.
Counting from the back, Aisha is 6th.

slips.say: 5 children are behind Aisha. Aisha is 6th: count her too.

tpl.q: There are {n} children in a line. Aisha is {f|ord} from the front. What place is Aisha from the back? Type just the number.
tpl.hint: Count from the back end: 1st, 2nd, and so on, up to Aisha.
steps: The places from the front and the back add to one more than the number of children.
{n} + 1 take away {f} is {ans}.
Aisha is {ans|ord} from the back.

items.q: Mei is 5th from the front and 5th from the back. How many children are in the line?
items.hint: Draw the line. Count the children in front of Mei, Mei herself and the children behind.
steps: 4 children are in front of Mei and 4 are behind.
It is not 10, because 5 + 5 counts Mei twice.

slips.say: 10 counts Mei twice. Count her only once.

tpl.q: Mei is {k|ord} from the front and {k|ord} from the back. How many children are in the line?
tpl.hint: Draw the line. Count the children in front of Mei, Mei herself and the children behind.
steps: {k} take away 1 children are in front of Mei, and the same number are behind.
Count Mei once: that is 2 times {k} take away 1.
There are {ans} children in the line.

items.q: Ali is 3rd and Mei is 9th in a line. How many children are between them?
items.hint: Say the places between: after the 3rd and before the 9th.
steps: The places between are 4th, 5th, 6th, 7th and 8th.
That is 5 children.

slips.say: 6 is 9 take away 3, which counts Mei. Between does not count Ali or Mei.

tpl.q: Ali is {a|ord} and Mei is {b|ord} in a line. How many children are between them?
tpl.hint: Say the places between: after the {a|ord} and before the {b|ord}.
steps: Take {a} from {b}, then take 1 more, because neither Ali nor Mei is between.
{b} take away {a} take away 1 is {ans}.
{ans} children are between them.

items.q: Ali is 3rd and Mei is 7th. List the places of the children between them. Type the numbers with a comma between.
items.hint: Count on from 3rd, but stop before 7th.
steps: After the 3rd comes the 4th.
Stop just before the 7th.
The places are 4, 5, 6.

slips.say: 3 and 7 are Ali and Mei. They are not between themselves.

items.q: A line has 13 children. Which place is the child in the middle? Type just the number.
items.hint: The middle child has the same number of children in front and behind.
steps: Take the middle child away. 12 children are left.
Half of 12 is 6 in front and 6 behind.
So the middle child is 7th.

slips.say: 6 children are in front of the middle child. The middle child is 7th.

tpl.q: A line has {n} children. Which place is the child in the middle? Type just the number.
tpl.hint: The middle child has the same number of children in front and behind.
steps: Take the middle child away. The other children make two equal groups.
Half of {n} take away 1 are in front of the middle child.
The middle child is {ans|ord}.

items.q: A line has 13 children. Mei is 4th from the front. Ben is 3rd from the back. How many children are between Mei and Ben?
items.hint: Find Ben's place from the front first. Then say the places between.
steps: Ben is 11th from the front, because 13 take away 3, add 1, is 11.
Between the 4th and the 11th are the 5th to the 10th.
That is 6 children.

slips.say: 7 is 11 take away 4. Between does not count Ben, so take away one more.

tpl.q: A line has {n} children. Mei is 4th from the front. Ben is 3rd from the back. How many children are between Mei and Ben?
tpl.hint: Find Ben's place from the front first. Then say the places between.
steps: Ben is {n} take away 3, add 1, from the front.
Between Mei (4th) and Ben are the places after the 4th and before Ben.
That is {ans} children.

items.q: Make up your own place puzzle for a grown-up. Give two clues and ask for the place of one child.
items.hint: Pick the answer first. Then write the clues.
steps: Check your puzzle with toys in a row.
Make sure the clues fit only one answer.
Ask a grown-up to solve it without looking at your answer.
